raw_response:
I am still doing the wheat-maize rotation on all 7.8 mu. My land is not much, and there are only two of us at home, so I cannot take big risks. What worked in past years is still the main thing. Wheat gives steady grain, and maize follows right after, same as most people here. If I spend too little on fertilizer, the crop looks weak and yield falls fast, but if I spend too much, the cash is tight, so this year I will use a middle amount, a little careful but not stingy. I have a well, so for wheat I will water at the important stages, and for maize I will give one irrigation if rain is not enough. Seed I will buy from the local dealer, the same kind neighbors often use, not the most expensive one. For pests, I do not spray blindly; I watch the field and use common herbicide and insecticide when needed.
